1.note: The pronoun **he** refers to David. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And David made houses for himself]

The author is most likely using the plural **houses** to mean a royal palace that had many different apartments for David’s wives and their children. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [a palace for himself that had apartments for his wives and their children]

2.q: לֹ֤א לָ⁠שֵׂאת֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָֽ⁠אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם כִּי־בָ֣⁠ם ׀ בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לָ⁠שֵׂ֞את אֶת־אֲר֧וֹן יְהוָ֛ה וּֽ⁠לְ⁠שָׁרְת֖⁠וֹ עַד־עוֹלָֽם
2.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Since Yahweh chose them to carry the Box of Yahweh and to serve him forever, one is not to carry the Box of God except the Levites]

2.q: לֹ֤א לָ⁠שֵׂאת֙ אֶת־אֲר֣וֹן הָֽ⁠אֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם
2.note: If it would appear in your language that Speaker was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [Only the Levites are to carry the Box of God]

3.note: The author is saying **all** as an overstatement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [people from throughout Israel]
To translate this expression and the similar ones in verses 12 and 28, see how you translated the similar expression in 11:6. Alternate translation: [to bring]

4.note: The author is describing these men as if they were actual **sons** of Aaron. He means that they were his descendants. The meaning of the term “sons” is the same in the rest of this chapter. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Aaron]

The author is describing the priests by reference to the fact that they were **sons** or descendants of **Aaron**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the priests]

5.note: To translate the term **brothers** here and in the rest of the chapter, see how you translated it in 5:7. Alternate translation: [and his kinsmen] or [and his relatives]

11.note: As 2 Samuel 8:16 and 2 Samuel 20:25 describe, **Zadok** and **Abiathar** served together as high priests during David’s reign. So the author is using the term **priests** to mean “high priests.” It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the high priests]

12.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֣אמֶר לָ⁠הֶ֔ם אַתֶּ֛ם רָאשֵׁ֥י הָ⁠אָב֖וֹת לַ⁠לְוִיִּ֑ם הִֽתְקַדְּשׁוּ֙ אַתֶּ֣ם וַ⁠אֲחֵי⁠כֶ֔ם וְ⁠הַֽעֲלִיתֶ֗ם אֵ֣ת אֲר֤וֹן יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶל־הֲכִינ֖וֹתִי לֽ⁠וֹ כִּ֛י לְ⁠מַ בָּ⁠רִ֥אשׁוֹנָ֖ה לֹ֣א אַתֶּ֑ם פָּרַ֨ץ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨י⁠נוּ֙ בָּ֔⁠נוּ כִּי־לֹ֥א דְרַשְׁנֻ֖⁠הוּ כַּ⁠מִּשְׁפָּֽט
12.note: If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine 15:12 and 15:13 into a verse bridge in order to put the reason that David gives before the result that he describes. Alternate translation: [And he said to them, “You are the heads of the fathers of the Levites. At the first, we did not seek Yahweh our God according to the ordinance, so it was not you, so he broke out against us. Therefore, consecrate yourselves, you and your brothers, and bring up the Box of Yahweh, the God of Israel, to {where} I have prepared for it]

The pronoun **them** refers both to the high priests and the Levites. David spoke to both groups at once, and some of what he said applied to both groups, specifically **Consecrate yourselves**, as verse 14 indicates. However, the rest of what David said applied only to the Levites, as they were supposed to carry the Box, as verse 2 indicates. But David summoned the high priests to hear his instructions to the Levites because the priests supervised the Levites in their work. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to those Levite leaders, with the high priests listening]

13.q: כִּ֛י לְ⁠מַ בָּ⁠רִ֥אשׁוֹנָ֖ה לֹ֣א אַתֶּ֑ם פָּרַ֨ץ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨י⁠נוּ֙ בָּ֔⁠נוּ
13.note: If you do not combine verses 12 and 13 into a verse bridge, you could still reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [You should do that because Yahweh our God broke out against us at the first because it was not you]

David is using **at the first** as a common expression of his culture to mean “the previous time.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the last time we tried this] or [the previous time]

David expects his listeners to understand that by **it was not you**, he means that it was not the Levites who carried the Box the previous time. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [it was not you who carried the Box]

David is speaking as if Yahweh actually **broke out** against the Israelites on the previous occasion, as if something had been containing him. (This image is similar to the one in 14:11.) If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Yahweh our God punished us]
In this context, the term **seek** describes being careful to obey. Alternate translation: [we were not careful to obey him as he required]

16.note: The author is speaking as if a **sound** were actually an object that people could **raise** If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to make a loud sound of rejoicing]

18.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “Ben.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation do not have this name. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

The author is using the adjective **seconds** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [the assistants]

19.note: The idea is not that these men would **make** these cymbals **hear** but that they would make people hear them. That is, they would play them loudly. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to play loudly]

20.note: The exact meaning of the word translated as **Alamoth** is uncertain. It may refer to (1) the pitch of the music. Alternate translation: [which they played in a high range] or (2) the tune of the song. Alternate translation: [on which they played the tune “Maidens”]

21.note: The exact meaning of the word translated as **Sheminith** is uncertain. It is related to the word for “eight.” (If you have already translated Psalm 6, see how you translated this term in the superscription to that psalm.) It may refer to (1) the pitch of the music. Alternate translation: [which they played an octave lower] or (2) the tune of the song. Alternate translation: [on which they played the tune “Sheminith”]

22.q: וּ⁠כְנַנְיָ֥הוּ שַֽׂר־הַ⁠לְוִיִּ֖ם בְּ⁠מַשָּׂ֑א יָסֹר֙ בַּ⁠מַּשָּׂ֔א כִּ֥י מֵבִ֖ין הֽוּא
22.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the phrase **in the carrying** at the start of the verse, since that seems to be a transition to a new topic, the transportation of the Box rather than the accompanying music. You could also put the reason **for he was understanding** before the result that Chenaniah was **to instruct about the carrying**. Alternate translation: [And as for the carrying, since Chenaniah, the chief of the Levites, was understanding, he was to instruct about the carrying]

The term **carrying** could describe: (1) the transportation of the Box. Alternate translation: [regarding the transportation of the Box … about its transportation] or (2) the music that the Levites were performing. (However, this is less likely, since verse 17 says that Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were responsible for directing the music.) Alternate translation: [regarding the music … about the music]

24.note: Here, **to the face of** represents “in front of.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of]

26.note: In this context, the term **helped** does not mean that God assisted the Levites in this task, for example, by giving them strength. It means that God did not punish them, as he had punished Uzzah on the previous occasion. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [when God did not punish the Levites]

The pronoun **they** probably does not refer immediately back to the **Levites** who were **carrying the Box**. They would not have interrupted that duty to offer sacrifices. Instead, the pronoun probably refers to their fellow Levites who were accompanying them. Alternate translation: [that their fellow Levites sacrificed]

In this culture, the number **seven** represented completeness and perfection. The Levites were profoundly grateful to Yahweh for sparing their lives as they transported this sacred object, and they were expressing complete, wholehearted gratitude. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text or in a footnote.

27.note: The expression **was clothed** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And David was wearing]

27.q: וְ⁠כָל־הַ⁠לְוִיִּם֙ הַ⁠נֹּשְׂאִ֣ים אֶת־הָ⁠אָר֔וֹן וְ⁠הַ⁠מְשֹׁ֣רְרִ֔ים וּ⁠כְנַנְיָ֛ה הַ⁠שַּׂ֥ר הַ⁠מַּשָּׂ֖א הַ⁠מְשֹֽׁרְרִ֑ים
27.note: The author is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and all of the Levites carrying the Box and the singers and Chenaniah, the chief of the carrying of the singers were also clothed in linen robes] or [and so were all of the Levites carrying the Box and the singers and Chenaniah, the chief of the carrying of the singers]

Here, the term **singers** seems to mean “Levites,” since the Levites as a group were singing on this occasion. It is possible that the specific Levites who were carrying the Box on poles on their shoulders were also singing. Alternate translation: [the Levites who were carrying the Box] or [the Levites who were singing as they carried the Box]

28.note: The author is saying **all** as an overstatement for emphasis. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a different way to express the emphasis. Alternate translation: [a great crowd of Israelites]

The author is not referring to a specific **shofar**. He means shofars in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [shofars]
